evidence: src/application/ports.ts declares IdGenerator.next() and Clock.now(). ProjectService, TaskService and UserService all receive them by constructor injection (CONSTRUCTOR_INJECTS edges), and none generates ids or times on its own.

src/application/dto.ts keeps all DTO mapping in one place (toUserDto, toProjectDto, toTaskDto, including the ISO date and null rules). project-service.ts, task-service.ts and user-service.ts return only these mapped DTOs.

src/application/task-service.ts: requireProject and the user lookup in assign repeat the existence checks in ProjectService.get and UserService.get. These are simple repository guards that throw NotFoundError, not a duplicated domain invariant.
src/application/task-service.ts hands state changes to the domain (task.assignTo, task.markDone(this.clock.now())), just as project-service.ts uses createProject and user-service.ts uses createUser.
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
This module passes. All five files belong to one application use-case layer for the project/task/user workflow: dto.ts holds the boundary DTOs and their mappers, ports.ts holds the infrastructure ports (IdGenerator, Clock), and there is one service per aggregate.

The services use the module's own abstractions consistently:
- Every service gets IdGenerator and Clock from ports.ts through constructor injection.
- No service calls Date or a UUID library directly.
- Every public method returns DTOs built by the shared mappers in dto.ts (toProjectDto, toTaskDto, toUserDto), so each serialization rule (ISO dates, null for optional fields) lives in one place.
- Domain logic is delegated to domain factories and methods (createProject, createUser, task.assignTo, task.markDone) instead of being reimplemented.

Two small overlaps exist, but neither is a duplicated invariant:
- TaskService.requireProject repeats the project-exists check from ProjectService.get.
- TaskService.assign repeats the user-exists check from UserService.get.

Each is a one-line repository lookup that throws NotFoundError, a normal guard for a use case that spans aggregates, not a business rule copied out of its home. TaskService builds tasks with `new Task({...})` while the other services call factory functions. That is a stylistic difference in how the domain is exposed, not a bypass of this module's own abstractions.
